 Phoenix Suns PHOENIX — The Phoenix Suns will officially have Luke Kennard tonight against the Golden State Warriors. 
--> PHOENIX — The Phoenix Suns will officially have Luke Kennard tonight against the Golden State Warriors. 
 "Yeah, seems to be going in the right direction," Suns head coach Jordan Ott said during his pre-game press conference. "I think he's on the court very soon here. So once that's completed and everything's in a good place, [we] hope to see him out there tonight."
--> "Yeah, seems to be going in the right direction," Suns head coach Jordan Ott said during his pre-game press conference. "I think he's on the court very soon here. So once that's completed and everything's in a good place, [we] hope to see him out there tonight."
 The Suns initially ruled Kennard questionable entering the weekend due to Left Knee Tendinopathy. He did not play in Phoenix's season opener in Portland on Wednesday after hurting his knee last week during preseason action. 
--> The Suns initially ruled Kennard questionable entering the weekend due to Left Knee Tendinopathy. He did not play in Phoenix's season opener in Portland on Wednesday after hurting his knee last week during preseason action. 
 Oso Ighodaro (Right Oblique Strain) and Mark Williams (Left Shoulder Surgery) were previously ruled out earlier today, so it was key for the Suns to get a prime three-point shooter added to their lineup to help offset their losses.

Kennard was the NBA's top three-point shooter last season, though Phoenix is hoping his low volume can increase. 
--> Kennard signed with Phoenix as a free agent this past summer to help replenish the team's three-point prowess lost with the Miles Bridges trade. Kennard was the NBA's top three-point shooter last season, though Phoenix is hoping his low volume can increase. 
 That's the hope with big names such as Devin Booker and Jalen Green in the backcourt, though the Suns see Kennard as much more than your typical spot-up shooter from deep.
